title: SRD coverage: snakes
summary: Independently authored GURPS builds for the 4 serpent identities issue #40 enumerates. Snakes split cleanly into two mechanical shapes and the batch keeps them apart: constrictors buy Constriction Attack and the ST to use it, and venomous snakes buy fangs and a disabling ability, with a bite that does almost nothing on its own. Size Modifier comes from the published table keyed to longest dimension, which for a serpent is its full length — a thirty-foot snake reads large on the table even though it is a hand's breadth wide, and the notes say so. ST comes from Basic Lift and from what the animal actually holds: a constrictor's coils have to beat the thing it is crushing.

monsters.name: Constrictor Snake
monsters.lair: A branch over a game trail, or a hollow under a root mass near water.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Backward-curved teeth that take hold rather than cut. The bite is how the coils arrive.

attacks.name: Constrict
attacks.notes: Once it has hold, the coils go on. No attack roll and no defense: win a Quick Contest of ST each second or take crushing damage and lose the breath to shout with.

monsters.description: Ten feet of muscle that has never needed venom. It lies along a branch with its head down at about head height, waiting for something warm to pass underneath. Everything turns on the first second. Before the coils it is a snake; after them it is arithmetic.
provenanceNotes: Ten feet, which is the SM +1 row.
ST from Basic Lift: the coils have to beat a struggling animal of its own mass, which is what constriction is.
The coils are priced by binding ST rather than by damage, because they do their work by holding rather than by wounding.

Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Double Jointed; the Tracking skill, which a creature with Discriminatory Smell should always have. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Giant Constrictor Snake
monsters.lair: A river bank undercut by the current, with a slide worn smooth into deep water.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Takes hold of an arm, a leg or a head and does not open again.

attacks.name: Constrict
attacks.notes: No attack roll and no defense once it has hold. Win a Quick Contest of ST each second or take crushing damage; a failure also costs the victim the ability to breathe, and drowning follows if the snake takes it into the water.

monsters.description: Thirty feet of river snake that swallows deer whole and sees no reason a person should be different. It comes out of brown water without a sound, takes hold with the jaws, and has three coils on before anyone upstream notices the splash. There is no trick to fighting it, only how fast the coils are cut.
provenanceNotes: Thirty feet, which is the SM +4 row. Note that this is a length reading: the animal is enormous end to end but no wider than a thigh, so it is easy to hit and hard to stop.
ST from Basic Lift: the coils have to beat a deer, and then a person who is pulling the other way.

Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: Double Jointed; the Tracking skill, which a creature with Discriminatory Smell should always have. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Giant Poisonous Snake
monsters.lair: A rock pile or ruin with sun on one side and a hole on the other.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Two punctures and almost no bleeding. Roll HT: on a failure the limb swells and darkens, the victim loses the use of it within minutes, and without treatment the swelling keeps traveling. This is the entire creature.

monsters.description: Ten feet of snake carrying enough venom to kill a horse, striking from a coil faster than a hand can be pulled back. It has no interest in a fight it cannot win by chemistry, so it warns first. The ones that do not warn are the ones that kill people.
provenanceNotes: Ten feet, which is the SM +1 row.

Weak in ST and deliberately so. The venom is priced at 40 points as a disabling ability, and it carries almost the whole rating; a bite that did meaningful damage as well would make this creature something it is not.

Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: the Tracking skill, which a creature with Discriminatory Smell should always have. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.

monsters.name: Viper Snake
monsters.lair: Leaf litter, a wood pile, or the warm stone beside a campfire.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Roll HT or lose the use of the bitten limb and take a slow, ugly wound that will not close. Untreated it is often fatal days later rather than minutes.

monsters.description: Under three feet, patterned into invisibility against dead leaves, and usually encountered by standing on it. A viper does not behave like a monster: it strikes once, it means it, and it leaves. The consequences arrive later, and they are what the party actually has to deal with.
notes: The 5.1 corpus prints this as 'Poisonous Snake' and the 3.5 corpus as 'Viper Snake'; both are this record.
provenanceNotes: About 3 feet, which is the SM -2 row.

Added after a post-hoc comparison against independent GURPS fan conversions of this creature: the Tracking skill, which a creature with Discriminatory Smell should always have. The comparison surfaced the gap; the build is still ours.
